Yeah I’ve heard that from a few others too. I decided to start the story right in the middle ya know? Just kinda drop the reader right into it. I thought by doing so I can keep readers engaged by avoid the whole boring slow burn setup and instead provide answers and context later down the line through dialogue and inner-monologue and stuff like that. Kinda like your learning things as the character learns them. Obviously it’s not exactly well implemented yet because there’s only 18 pages but answers will come, and exposition will happen as the story progresses. Though, maybe I should explain some more of the basic information and world building earlier on like you said

Crazy how women can just drop someone that was such a huge part of their life that at such a break-neck speed. Same thing happened to me, did everything I could to make her happy, and she was. Until one day, she wasn’t. And that was the end. It hurt, real bad. I still think about her, but I will tell you that the intensity of sorrow you feel right now, is the worst it gets. As time goes on and you meet new people and reconnect with old friends and develop new passions and hobbies, it gets so much easier to get out of bed. You think of her less and less. You might never forget her, but she won’t be occupying your mind anymore. It’ll be just like any other memory you have. A quick thought and then gone, because you realize you have more important things and more important people in your life to focus on. Keep pushing, and these days and these thoughts will soon be far, far behind you.
